questions.ask: What are the last four digits of your account number?

intents.hardship: The customer mentions financial hardship: job loss, illness, bereavement, being unable to afford essentials.
intents.dispute: The customer says 'This is not my debt' or 'I never had this product'.
intents.already_paid: The customer says 'I have already paid'.
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan, a restructuring or lower instalments.
intents.vague: A vague time instead of a date, such as 'soon' or 'after payday'.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.
intents.human: A request to speak to a human.

lines.opening: Good day, this is Isla, Corran Bank's automated assistant. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am an automated assistant.
lines.scam: You can check by calling the number on the back of your card.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain once I have confirmed that I am speaking with the right person.

lines.not_talk_once: I understand. This will only take a few minutes.

lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with {first_name} {last_name}.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. We will call {first_name} back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry to have troubled you.
lines.condolence: I am very sorry for your loss.
lines.id_intro: Before I go on, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_why: I ask these questions to protect your account.
lines.id_explain: These questions protect your account, so I need the answers before I can go on.
lines.id_declined: I understand, but I can't go on without the answers.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you say it again, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't confirm your identity. Please call the number on the back of your card or visit a branch.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you. I am calling about a late payment.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} past due, and it is {days} days late.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full amount today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full amounts today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. Could you pay {amount} on {date} instead?
lines.offer_floor: I understand. Could you pay {amount} instead?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't record an amount that low. The lowest I can record is {floor}. Could you pay that?
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, that is still below the lowest amount I can record.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed. Could you give me a date from today onwards?
lines.not_business_day: I'm sorry, that is not a business day. Could you pay on {date} instead?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can record is {date}. Could you pay on that day?
lines.vague_ask: Could you give me an exact date?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay that?
lines.repeat_offer: To repeat, could you pay {amount} on {date}?

lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise is recorded.
lines.sms_line: You will receive a confirmation by text message.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, your promise could not be recorded because of a system problem.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take two business days to show.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't ask you for a payment on this call.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that. I'll put you through to our care team, who can help.
lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to a colleague who can help with that.
lines.human_ask_help: I may be able to help you myself. Is there something I can help with?
lines.transfer: Please hold while I transfer you.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, the promise can't be changed on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book the callback.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer didn't go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Is that correct, yes or no?

lines.no_band_line: I'm sorry, I can't take a promise for your {name} on this call.

assumptions: Opening: the brief's first sentence ends with 'This call is recorded.' The spec format keeps the word 'recorded' for the promise lines only and requires the active voice, so the opening says 'We record this call.' The format rule is the more specific instruction. The rest of the brief's first sentence is kept word for word.
The call data has no title. confirm_ask uses the brief's exact words 'Is this {first_name} {last_name}?' and there are no extra call variables.

Amounts: get_account gives past_due, minimum_due and monthly_instalment in pounds, so amounts are spoken in pounds. create_promise takes a whole-number amount in pence (rule 32 and the API: 85.50 pounds is 8550). amount_scale is therefore 100, for the amount sent to create_promise.
Calendar: business days are Monday to Friday except the five Corran Bank holidays listed. Weekends and those holidays are the non-business days.
date_rules.next_weekday: the brief does not define 'next <weekday>', so the default following_week is kept.
Confirmation (rule 2): the question is asked at most twice. If the answer is still unclear after the second ask, the call ends as unclear.

Callback (rules 5-6): only on a business day that is today or one of the next two business days, from 09:30 to 18:00 with both ends included, and strictly later than now. After a slot outside these rules the agent asks once more (max_asks 2). If the second slot is also outside, nothing is booked (no_callback).

Identity (rules 9-12): postcode first, then account_last4. Two wrong answers in total, on either question, end the check (the brief and the API agree), so max_wrong is 2 with no per-question limit. The postcode is sent in capitals with every space removed and has no fixed length, because UK postcodes vary. account_last4 is sent as exactly four digits with leading zeros kept.
date_order: this brief asks no date question, so the default dmy is kept.
The verify_identity response has no hint field, so identity.hints is empty and response.hint is ''. verified is a boolean, so pass_values and reject_values are empty.

purpose_is_decline (true) and question_is_decline (false): the brief does not say, so the defaults are kept. Rule 12: the agent says once that the questions protect the account, and a second refusal means identity is declined.

Floor (rule 22): minimum_due for credit_card and overdraft, monthly_instalment for personal_loan. If that field is higher than past_due, the floor is past_due. The brief gives no spoken name for the floor, so it is named from the fields: 'minimum amount due' and 'monthly instalment'.

Deadlines (rules 16-19): early (1-10) is the 8th business day after today, with today not counted. Middle (11-30) is today plus 14 calendar days, moved forward to the next business day if needed, so rules.deadline_adjust is next_business_day. Late (31-60) is the last calendar day of the current month, moved back to the last business day. It is written as last_business_day_of_month so the forward adjustment never applies to it. If that business day is earlier than today, the last business day of next month is used, found the same way.

Ladder (rule 26), set per band. Attempt 1 is the full amount on the first business day after today, or on the deadline if that is earlier (the next_business_day date is capped at the deadline). Middle attempt 2 is the floor on the deadline. Late attempt 2 is the full amount on the deadline, and late attempt 3 is the floor on the deadline. Full-amount steps are full_or_floor because, once the customer says the full amount is too much, every proposal uses the floor (rule 24). The top-level ladder repeats the late ladder.

Rule 27: a step that would repeat an earlier proposal's amount and date exactly is skipped, and the customer is not asked again. When the ladder is used up, the customer has refused (rule 29). The last step is not repeated (ladder_repeat_last false).
too_much_floor asked_date: the floor is offered once, on the date of the current proposal, and uses no attempt. Refusing the floor is a flat refusal (rule 24).
first_ask today: 'Can you pay the full amount today?' is neither a proposal nor a persuasion attempt (rule 25).
refuse_deadline_is_refusal true: a plain no to the deadline offered under rule 20 is a no with no date and no amount, which is a flat refusal (rule 26).

Promise dates: today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline (rule 15). If the customer names a non-business day, the agent offers the next business day, or the deadline if that is earlier. A date after the deadline gets the deadline (rule 20). A vague time gets one request for an exact date, then counts as a flat refusal (rule 21). A date or amount the customer names is never a refusal (rule 28).

Hardship (rule 37): one sentence of sympathy, no proposal, and a transfer to queue care. The brief transfers without offering, so the hardship line announces the transfer. Both events.hardship and events.transfer_support close as transferred / hardship with no note.
Payment plan (rule 38) transfers to payment_plans without describing anything. A human request (rule 39) transfers to customer_service after the agent asks once whether it can help.

Notes: add_note is written just before close_call, and only for already paid (claims_paid), refused (customer_refused), dispute (disputed) and system failure (system_failure). The optional add_note text field is not sent. close_call sends no reason for promise_made and already_paid (the table says 'none').
System failure (rule 33): create_promise is tried once more after a failure. A second failure is service_error.
after_promise.ask_anything_else (true), max_not_talk (2) and the multi settings: the brief does not cover them and covers one product only, so the defaults are kept.
callback_requested is left out: the brief does not say what to do when a verified customer asks to be called back.
bands_outside is null: the brief only calls customers who are 1 to 60 days late and gives no rule for other values.
promise_change: the brief does not say, so the agent says the promise cannot be changed on this call.

The optional products list_field, id_field and type_field, and responses, are left to the tool API file. get_account returns a single 'product' object with product_id and type, and every tool reports success with the boolean 'ok'.
